proof_summary: Take the composite counterexample \(n=p^2\) with \(p=16843\); a modular reciprocal-sum computation shows \(H_{p-1}\equiv0\pmod{p^3}\). Splitting \(H_{p^2-2}-1\) into terms whose indices are multiples of \(p\) and the remaining terms, the former equal \(p^{-1}H_{p-1}\), while pairing each latter index \(k\) with \(p^2-k\) supplies a factor \(p^2\); hence \(v_p(H_{p^2-2}-1)\ge2\), so \(p^2\) divides the reduced numerator-minus-denominator despite \(p^2\) being composite.
